title: Two-stage launch for a new brand, location or product line
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: How to launch so buyers first learn what category it is, then build memory and availability over time.
applies_when: New brand, location, product line or variant
exclusions: Established brand in a well-understood category (positioning work instead)
evidence_requirements: Evidence the offer works for buyers (tests, pilots)
Overlap between the new offer's buyers and the parent's buyers, and other comparable offers' overlap with the parent (for cannibalisation)
Reasons for non-repeat, gathered with neutral wording
missing_data_behavior: No budget: owner's own channels only.
implementation_steps: Priority memories: say what it is (category cue), how it looks and where to buy
Make the name clear and early in every execution; start building assets
Borrow existing cultural or category cues
Spread spend across months; avoid burst-then-silence
Monitor rejection with neutral questions, including 'couldn't find it' or 'didn't see it'
dependencies: The product has been tested with buyers. The book assumes pre-testing; if that's missing, validation comes first (PB-concierge, PB-interviews)

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: Enough to sustain presence beyond launch week
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: First-time buyers per month; repeat by quarter; rejection reasons; overlap with parent

metrics: Overlap with the parent versus the benchmark
guardrails: Launch-presence duration is a policy decision for the owner, not a book rule.
Don't rely on influencers or 'opinion leaders' as the main mechanism
Don't lead with differentiation before the category is clear
Don't treat low early repeat as rejection without evidence
alternatives_when_constrained: No overlap data: skip the cannibalisation benchmark and track total sales across parent and variant
stop_conditions: Review after 1 and 2 quarters: penetration trend, repeat and rejection reasons
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Products needing demonstration (disruptive innovation), where WOM and in-person demos matter more

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: Launch plans keep a presence for at least the first three months after launch week; the three-month span is ClimbOS policy, not from the book.

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: Launch messaging states the category, name, look and where to buy before any differentiation claim.
proposed: Flag cannibalisation only when overlap with the parent exceeds the average sharing of comparable offers by about 10 points (the authors' rule of thumb).
proposed: Low early repeat is labelled 'expected for a new brand' and investigated with neutral rejection questions before product changes.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: If product-market fit isn't evidenced, the plan leads with validation; the book assumes a tested product.
